newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-CAMPESE OPENS FINAL TOUR WITH TRY.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-CAMPESE OPENS FINAL TOUR WITH TRY.

text.p: David Campese, the world's record test try-scorer, opened his final tour with a try on Saturday as Australia defeated a Glasgow-Edinburgh combined side 37-19.

Winger Campese, who missed the tour opener against Scotland A last Wednesday, gave the final perfectly-timed pass after the ball had moved swiftly along the line to send fly-half David Knox in for a try on the stroke of half-time.
He then got on the scorecard himself shortly after the interval, jogging over the line after a clever intrusion from full-back Joe Roff.
Australia dominated the line-outs and used the rolling maul to telling effect in driving rain after the combined side had taken the early lead through a penalty from fly-half Allie Donaldson.
Knox levelled with a similar effort after six minutes and the scores were tied until the 28th minute when Donaldson was again successful.

Mark Connors, who drove over for a try against Scotland A, scored with a similar effort and although another Donaldson penalty reduced the margin Knox's try enabled the tourists to go into the interval 15-9 ahead.
A fourth penalty to Donaldson kept the combined team in touch and a determined run from captain Scott Hastings was rewarded with a try to Scotland winger Kenny Logan.
But Campese's try and further scores to Daniel Manu and captain Dave Wilson kept the Wallabies firmly in command.
Hastings conceded the 5-1 try tally in favour of Australia had been a fair reflection of the game while Campese said the tourists were still finding their feet.
"We are just trying to get our combinations," he said. "We are still feeling our way."
